items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: I said, you bring a name band and it's going to cost you an awful lot of money. I said, I'll get you a name leader, Ray Teal.

ctx.x: I bought a half interest in many tunes just to get it off my back.

Because he was always, he'd steal an orchestration of Dave Frank and sell it to me. He came over to Biloxi when someone was playing at the Buena Vista and he puts his head in the door and he says, hey Pops. Oh I said, my God, I got this guy on my hands all summer. He came in with his clothes wrapped in the newspaper. But I wasn't eating in the hotel because I had taken a cottage because I was expecting visitors. So I told him, I said I'm entitled to three meals a day. I said please give them to this fellow. So…

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: So he led the band. But he only wanted one trumpet. He didn't care for brass. But he had three violins, and it was all I played with. And four saxes, piano, bass violin, and I played trombone. And I was the only brass.

ctx.x: And they wanted an attraction. And I didn't want to lose the job because the job is a job. And I'm talking about the things that are tough. And I was a leader, getting a leader. So I said, well I changed the band. People are like this and they're like me. I said, I'll get you a leader, Ray Teal. I said, he's been at the sangha, he's been a master summer, he plays saxophone. And I was like, I'm a master of the band. And I said, well get him. So I got Ray Teal, we were good friends, we used to make out for a month.…
